runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner carrying 135lbs, with a 14-day turnaround for Kubler's yard (2 from 9 at the meeting); five runs on similar going with one win and two places, and her 7f Good ground win last time out gives confidence she can replicate that effort over this extra furlong.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this prominent racer who won at 7f on Soft and has a 34-day freshener; the step back to similar ground after a below-par run is the key angle, though the 16-race sequence on Good showing zero wins is a concern for punters looking for value.

runners_data.name: Mr Nugget
runners_data.note: David Simcock's five-year-old returns after a 121-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — and his form shows consistent placing at 8f on the all-weather; the switch to turf on Good to Firm is an unknown factor but Muscutt is a capable booking and his finishing positions suggest he stays well.

runners_data.name: War Chant
runners_data.note: A natural front-running type whose genuine inclination to race prominently has been pushed back in this map due to the volume of pace already present; back after 189 days and his stable running at 2/17 over 14 days, though the drop to 8f from his recent 10f-11f form over the all-weather is an interesting angle worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up performer fitted with a tongue-tie who has run to near-identical form figures in recent outings (4-2-2-4); the consistency on Good and Standard ground is reassuring and Ghiani's booking adds confidence, but the 14-day return means he is race-fit and his two placed efforts on Good ground are directly relevant here.

runners_data.name: Rogue Dynasty
runners_data.note: James Owen's yard is in exceptional form (11 from 48 over 14 days), and Rogue Dynasty's five-run history on Good ground has produced a win and four places, making him statistically the most ground-consistent runner in the race; the 23-day gap is ideal and Harry Davies keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes the mount on this genuine hold-up performer who is fitted with a tongue-tie; his natural style of racing from the rear means he needs a strong enough pace to close into, and with only one confirmed front-runner he risks the race not truly unfolding in his favour despite a solid two-placed effort on Good ground at 8f.

races.paceDynamic: Distinct Spirit is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, she should settle into an uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat mile. The pace will be honest but controlled — Distinct Spirit has winning form over 7f on Good ground and will not be bullied into a false rhythm, meaning the early fractions are likely to be measured rather than scorching. Drifts Away and Mr Nugget will push to track from prominent positions, ensuring the race is not run in slow motion, but the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. This shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly through a steady gallop and produce a sustained late run, provided the early pace is fast enough to string the field out — Panelli, Rogue Dynasty and Man Of Desert all sit in that profile. The field contains more prominent-leaning types than the shape can accommodate: War Chant is a natural prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield, and Distinct Spirit herself is the most likely of all to actually secure and hold the front position throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Distinct Spirit Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit leads unchallenged and sets a fair but manageable tempo, allowing her to dictate from the front.
scenarios.body: Distinct Spirit settles into a rhythm with Drifts Away and Mr Nugget tracking behind, and the steady gallop preserves enough in the tank for the leader to repel closers late on Good to Firm ground. Front-runners and prominent racers who travel economically benefit most when the pace is honest but not punishing, and Distinct Spirit's 7f win on Good ground suggests she has the finishing reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sufficient to stretch the field and the hold-up horses get a clean run through into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Rogue Dynasty and Panelli, both proven on Good ground in recent outings, can close powerfully if the tempo has been brisk enough to create a gap, while Man Of Desert's true hold-up style means he ideally needs this shape to deliver. The flat Yarmouth track with no undulations suits a sustained gallop finish, giving closers a genuine chance if the front-runners have used themselves up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit fades in the final furlong and the race opens up for horses tracking in the middle of the pack.
scenarios.body: War Chant, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution rather than true preference, could benefit from an unexpectedly fast early pace that sees the front runners weaken; his stamina over 10f suggests the mile may bring out a late effort. Mr Nugget, who has won at 8f on the all-weather with a prominent style, is best placed of the genuine mid-packers to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dawdle Then Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a tactical crawl and the race becomes a sprint finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo would compress the field and hand the advantage to the horse with the sharpest turn of foot over a short distance, which potentially disadvantages the hold-up types who need a true run. Drifts Away, who won on Soft ground and whose recent form includes a win at 7f, may have enough pace for a sprint finish, though this shape suits nobody cleanly in this field.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Dynasty's trainer James Owen is running at a 23% strike-rate over the past 14 days — if he travels well in mid-to-rear, watch for the sustained run that his Good-ground form strongly suggests.

Man Of Desert is a genuine hold-up horse mapped closer to midfield due to redistribution — if De Sousa cannot get him settled in his true rearward position, his race will be compromised from the outset.

War Chant returns after 189 days for a yard running at 2/17 over the meeting — significant absence and trainer form dip mean any early-race sluggishness should be noted, particularly if he fails to find his natural prominent position.

Distinct Spirit carries top weight (135lbs) and is the sole confirmed pace-setter; if she is slow into stride or loses the lead at any stage, the race shape collapses entirely and the hold-up horses become the primary beneficiaries.

Mr Nugget reappears after 121 days off the track — watch his early behaviour and how quickly Muscutt finds him a position, as a horse returning cold from a long break on a flat, unforgiving Good to Firm surface can either strip fit or show ring-rust at the crucial moment.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Starfinch
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner for Harry Eustace, last seen 82 days ago and returning with a dismal record on similar going (0 wins, 0 places from 4 attempts); Kaiya Fraser will need a much stronger pace than expected to have any hope of delivering a telling late run in a field this small.

runners_data.name: Caviar Cowboy
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has strong recent form at this trip on Tapeta (two wins, multiple places) and Daniel Muscutt gets the dream front-running brief in a four-runner heat; going is fine, trip is proven, and the lone lead role means no fight for the front.

runners_data.name: Three Non Blondes
runners_data.note: Hayley Burton's trainer strike rate over 14 days is a concern (0/2), and Marco Ghiani inherits a horse that is a natural prominent type whose best recent form came at 7f on Good — it needs something to go wrong for the front two to get involved.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas's colt is the standout on form figures for this trip and going combination (placed six times from seven runs on similar ground, two wins), and though Tom Marquand will be unable to secure his preferred prominent position with Caviar Cowboy asserting early, his ability to track just off the pace makes him the most credible challenger.

races.paceDynamic: Caviar Cowboy is the lone confirmed front-runner and, in a field of just four, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — expect a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth's flat, undemanding 7f. Three Non Blondes and Hardy's Hero are both natural prominent racers, but with Caviar Cowboy already taking the rail position, at least one of them will be unable to slot where they want, creating mild positional friction in the early stages without meaningfully pressuring the pace. Starfinch is the one true hold-up runner but has a poor recent record — nine runs without a win in similar going conditions — making its late challenge speculative at best. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred ground: Caviar Cowboy is overwhelmingly best-placed to control from the front, with Hardy's Hero most likely to settle just off the pace in a comfortable position given Tom Marquand's experience managing horses in small fields. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable tempo — strongly favours Caviar Cowboy to dictate and prove difficult to peg back, with the player best positioned to exploit any fade being Hardy's Hero tracking just off the shoulder.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caviar Cowboy Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Caviar Cowboy leads without pressure and sets a fair but manageable tempo on the Good to Firm surface.
scenarios.body: Caviar Cowboy dictates every yard from the front, keeping the pace honest enough to prevent a sustained closing challenge from the rear, and simply finds another gear when asked in the final furlong. The front-runner's profile is perfectly suited: small field, no rival willing to chase, and an OR of 85 backed by a recent course win at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hardy's Hero Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Caviar Cowboy sets too strong a pace and Hardy's Hero travels sweetly just off the leader to reel it in late.
scenarios.body: Hardy's Hero's recent form — placed in six of its last seven, including multiple seconds and thirds at 7f on Good — marks it as the most likely beneficiary of any pace collapse. Tom Marquand can nurse it into a challenging position approaching the final two furlongs, and its consistent finishing suggests it handles this test well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Three Non Blondes Grabs A Share
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and Three Non Blondes, tracking behind the leader, runs on to take a place or snatch the race.
scenarios.body: Three Non Blondes has at least some form at this trip and going combination (placed twice from six similar-going starts) and Marco Ghiani can exploit a tactical opportunity if the front two tie each other up. However, the trainer's 14-day strike rate is weak (0/2) and this profile depends on conditions not currently pointing its way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Starfinch Late Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Starfinch — the sole true hold-up runner — finds clear running to deliver a sustained finish.
scenarios.body: Starfinch would need an unusually strong gallop, a clear passage, and a reversal of its recent form (zero wins, zero places in four similar-going starts) to factor at all. This scenario is heavily discounted: Starfinch's style fit is genuine but its recent record on similar going is uninspiring, and in a field of only four, gaps may not materialise.

watchPoints.text: Watch Caviar Cowboy's early sections — if Daniel Muscutt sends it straight to the front without a challenge, the race shape is effectively set within the first furlong and any hold-up runner's chance narrows sharply.

Hardy's Hero may not get its natural prominent pitch with Caviar Cowboy dominating the front: watch how Tom Marquand settles it in the first two furlongs, as an unsettled early position could undermine its otherwise strong place claims.

Three Non Blondes showed signs of temperament in its last two outings — if Marco Ghiani cannot secure a clean early rhythm, its moderate recent form (including a seventh last time) suggests it could drop away tamely.

Starfinch's 82-day absence and zero from four in similar going are the most notable flags in the field — watch for signs of freshness early, but treat any midrace move with scepticism given its form profile.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f trip at Yarmouth in similar going and is the race's sole pace-maker; his STYLE_FIT tag reflects a slight positional nuance but he has proven front-running credentials here, and an uncontested lead on fast ground suits him ideally — the key question is whether he can sustain the effort over the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Mercury Day
runners_data.note: Blinkers-wearing hold-up specialist who has been finishing off races from the rear over 6-7f in similar ground; Jack Gilligan takes the mount for a trainer with a quiet recent strike rate, and from naturally further back on a straight track he needs a truly honest pace to bring his finishing kick into play.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa partners this consistent prominent racer who has placed multiple times at this trip and on similar ground; she is the most likely horse to press Mr Ubiquitous early, and her recent record of 3-2-1-4-5 shows she competes at the business end — her challenge depends on bridging the gap to the front-runner under her own steam.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides a horse whose form string shows five consecutive placed efforts without a win, making him a reliable but perhaps not decisive closer; his record in similar Good ground is solid (six runs, five placed), yet his inability to win from hold-up suggests he needs others to set up a strong pace he can exploit late.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose true rear-of-field style is somewhat disguised by his midfield mapping — the field simply has too many hold-up types for all to show at the back; wearing a visor and last seen 12 days ago, his recent form (740760) makes it hard to trust him at the business end even if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: David Simcock's lightly-weighted four-year-old carries a 15lb pull on several rivals off OR 59, and two wins from five runs show real ability; he is a natural hold-up type shown in midfield due to redistribution — his race hinges on the pace being fast enough that his lighter burden tells late, which is possible but far from guaranteed against more exposed rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Ubiquitous is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, controlling tempo on the Yarmouth straight mile over 7f on Good to Firm ground. Berry Clever will likely press from a prominent position, but with a STYLE_FIT caveat suggesting she may be racing slightly out of her ideal role, she is unlikely to apply serious early pressure sufficient to unsettle Mr Ubiquitous's rhythm. The hold-up contingent — Mercury Day, Rogue Allegiance, North View, and Campani — will be forced to track from varying degrees of distance, with North View and Campani redistributed into midfield despite being natural hold-up types, meaning the rear of the field may be more tightly bunched than the map implies. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: an uncontested pace-setter on a flat, straight track with fast ground creates the classic scenario where the leader controls the fractions, and only a horse able to race forwardly or pick up from a close-up position has a realistic chance of pegging them back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ubiquitous Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ubiquitous is allowed to stride clear early and dictate a sustainable pace from the front without pressure.
scenarios.body: He sets his own fractions on the Yarmouth straight, building a lead that proves beyond the hold-up horses on fast ground over a trip that suits a front-runner dictating the race. Prominent types positioned close behind are best placed to benefit if he falters late, but the controlled tempo makes him extremely difficult to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Catch Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Mr Ubiquitous is genuinely fast enough that he ties up late, allowing closers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Mercury Day or Rogue Allegiance, tracking from behind, find the burst of pace required in the final furlong as the leader empties out under the pressure of his own fractions. This is the main counter-scenario but requires the pace to be materially quicker than a lone front-runner typically sets when uncontested.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Home
scenarios.trigger: If Berry Clever presses Mr Ubiquitous from early on and the two fight it out in a sustained duel to the line.
scenarios.body: A genuine battle up front raises the pace enough to stretch the field, and the winner emerges from the leading pair who have spent the most time in the race. Hold-up horses lack the ground to close in time on the straight Yarmouth layout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Campani, running off an OR of 59 with a dramatically lower weight, produces a rare front-to-mid run on fast ground and catches the principals flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Despite being a natural hold-up type redistributed into midfield, Campani's lower handicap weight and recent winning form at this trip could allow her to make late inroads if the main contenders' pace collapses. This requires multiple things to go wrong for the principals and is the least likely of the four shapes.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Berry Clever's jockey Silvestre De Sousa attempts to press Mr Ubiquitous immediately after the start — if she does, the pace lifts sharply and hold-up horses gain a genuine late-race opportunity.

North View and Campani are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; if both drift back to their natural position, the genuine hold-up group is larger than the race map suggests and the pace may not be fast enough to bring them into it.
Rogue Allegiance has placed five times without winning in recent form — monitor whether Harry Davies elects to ride more aggressively than usual given his runner's tendency to find not enough late.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race, identical to earlier races on the card — fast ground favours Mr Ubiquitous's front-running style on the straight Yarmouth track and does not typically help hold-up horses who need cut to close the gap.

Campani's significant weight advantage (120lbs vs 133-135lbs for rivals) could become a factor if the race truly develops into a stamina test in the final furlong, making him worth tracking visually even if his natural style is compromised by his starting position.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Maith Mar Or
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a placing over 10f on Good in the book; trainer John Berry has gone 0/4 in the past 14 days, and she carries a big weight burden of 142lbs which is a material concern in a sprint-finish scenario on Good to Firm over this trip.

runners_data.name: Gretna Dreams
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good earlier in her career and Marco Ghiani is an excellent judge of pace, but she is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot — the 32-day absence and her recent string of poor finishes (7-7-6-6) make it hard to trust her even if the sprint-finish shape suits in theory.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by a stamina influence who has run consistently mid-pack without threatening; Billy Loughnane takes over for Michael Bell and the horse has never won in four attempts, though his two placings on Good ground suggest he handles conditions and could pick up a minor share in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Caraway
runners_data.note: Took a maiden over 12f on Good and followed up with a placed effort over 14f at Salisbury, showing genuine form at this distance band; ran just yesterday which is an unusual turnaround for Haggas and Tom Marquand rides, but his natural hold-up style in a field of closers means he must rely on the sprint-finish shape delivering accurately.

runners_data.name: Twilight Guest
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran who wears a hood and has finished no better than fourth in his last six, with 11 places from 15 starts on Good ground suggesting consistency without a cutting edge; George Margarson's yard is 0/8 in the 14-day window and the lowest OR in the field at 46 makes him a stiff ask even if the flat, fast conditions are superficially acceptable.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up profile, nobody wants to lead at Yarmouth over 1m3½f on Good to Firm ground, creating a race that will crawl into the straight before igniting into a sprint finish off a falsely-run, compressed tempo. The likely outcome is a dawdling first mile with the field bunched together, jockeys watching each other, before a sharp three-furlong dash from the home turn decides the outcome. This race shape unambiguously favours the horse with the highest cruising speed and the ability to quicken from a compact group — raw finishing pace over stamina. All three runners tagged as redistributed — Caraway, Gretna Dreams, and Twilight Guest — are genuine hold-up types nudged into the midfield slots on the map simply because every horse in this field prefers to race off the pace, meaning none is truly equipped to dominate from the front should the tactical vacuum demand it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Off Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls for the first mile and the race ignites into a three-furlong dash from the turn, favouring the horse with the sharpest acceleration.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace-maker, the tempo will be pedestrian and the race will compress into a contest decided by pure sprint speed over the final quarter-mile; horses that can quicken on a flat, fast surface will dominate. Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth rewards those with a quick stride rather than grinding stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Horse Breaks Early
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey elects to force the pace from the outset to avoid being trapped in a wall-to-wall sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A horse sent forward unexpectedly gains a significant positional advantage and controls the fractions, potentially stealing a march on a flat galloping track where cover is hard to find. The winner here would be whoever has the tactical intelligence and fitness to sustain that lead around a wide, exposed circuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely brisk enough to string the field out and the race is won by a strong-finishing hold-up horse who picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: This scenario is undermined by the fact that all hold-up horses here are naturally suited to exactly this but none will have the space or the tempo to truly exploit a closing run, making a clean late swoop difficult to execute. The redistributed runners Gretna Dreams and Twilight Guest would be the theoretical beneficiaries, but their STYLE_FIT discount reduces the probability materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles throughout with multiple jockeys refusing to commit, producing a messy, error-strewn finish with no clear winner profile.
scenarios.body: In a race where every runner is a hold-up type and nobody imposes rhythm, the result becomes a lottery decided by track position in the final furlong rather than genuine ability. Lower-rated horses such as Twilight Guest could flatter in this scenario if they happen to secure a fortunate wide run, though this remains the least likely and least repeatable outcome.

watchPoints.text: With all five runners hold-up types, watch for a dangerously slow early tempo — any horse that drifts wide on the home turn without cover could find itself with too much ground to make up in the sprint.
Caraway ran yesterday and Haggas rarely turns horses around this quickly; monitor paddock condition and early market moves for any signs the horse is below peak freshness heading into this race.

Gretna Dreams is mapped to midfield but is a natural hold-up racer — if the field bunches tightly at the halfway point she may find herself boxed in and unable to find her natural rhythm, compounding her recent poor form.

Maith Mar Or carries the highest weight in the field at 142lbs on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth, a flat, fast track that emphasises stride quality — monitor whether the burden visibly affects her action in the closing stages of a sprint finish.
Twilight Guest's hood is worth tracking in the paddock; if he is unsettled or reluctant to settle in the early dawdle, his finishing effort in a compressed sprint will be compromised further.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chasing Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid recent form figures of 3-3 who has placed on similar going; 31 days fresh suits this flat track, and with a gelding hood on, Michael Keady's runner may creep into contention from mid-division rather than the rear as intended.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two wins and five places in 15 starts on similar going including a Yarmouth second over this exact 6f trip; Tom Marquand takes the ride but this horse is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot by the volume of closers — its chance depends on a stronger pace than this field is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: One For Harvey
runners_data.note: Returning after 287 days off for Clare Hobson, whose trainer T14 figures (0/5) do little to inspire confidence; a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield by redistribution, and the combination of a long absence and an overcrowded hold-up division makes this a significant risk at any price.

runners_data.name: Havana Jag
runners_data.note: Unknown early style in a field lacking genuine pace — likely to default into a front or prominent position by circumstance rather than design; Kaiya Fraser has ridden the horse recently and its consistent placed record (four times in the top four from 11 starts on similar ground) suggests it handles good-to-firm well enough to capitalise on a false pace.

runners_data.name: Ballsgrove Boy
runners_data.note: Back after 271 days for Peter Chapple-Hyam and has been consistently beaten in handicaps at this level over 6f on standard and softer surfaces; Silvestre De Sousa's booking adds interest but the horse's hold-up style, pushed toward midfield by the crowded closer profile, and its form figures of 9-7-7-7-12 on standard ground are hard to excuse.

runners_data.name: Charging Bull
runners_data.note: Wears hood and has a modest but consistent record with a recent placed effort; a natural hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield means it will likely be caught between two positions in a race with no true leader setting an honest pace, making its chance harder to land than the style mismatch alone suggests.

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old runs in a tongue-strap and has placed at Yarmouth over 6f on good ground previously — the standout course-and-distance relevant piece of form in this field; hold-up by tendency, but with Billy Loughnane's positive booking and a stable showing 5/20 in the past fortnight, it merits respect as a natural closer with genuine course form.

runners_data.name: Rianka
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly wearing a tongue-tie for Martin Dunne, who has shown consistency over 6f at Yarmouth on good and good-to-firm ground across her short form string; Marco Ghiani rides and her light weight is an asset, though as another redistributed hold-up type in a field without a genuine pacemaker, finding a clear run from the rear could prove problematic.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 6f handicap at Yarmouth, and all eight runners carrying a hold-up or unknown style designation, there is no horse clearly tasked with setting the pace from the front — meaning the early stages are likely to be messy, slow-burning, and contested by default rather than design. Havana Jag (style=U) is the most likely candidate to end up on or near the lead simply by process of elimination, with Chasing Gold and Blindfold Games both hold-up types who may find themselves closer to the pace than usual on good-to-firm ground over a flat 6f. The absence of any genuine front-runner compresses the field into a tight sprint finish where the race is likely to be truly run from the two-furlong pole, suiting horses with a finishing kick rather than those who need to make their move from further back. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Due Date, One For Harvey, Ballsgrove Boy, Charging Bull, and Rianka have all been redistributed to midfield, but the horses most likely to actually press forward into a lead role are Havana Jag and, by default, whichever of the hold-up types breaks smartest; the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-pace runners who can exploit any early dawdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early with no genuine leader and the race ignites only in the final two furlongs, compressing the finish.
scenarios.body: Havana Jag drifts into a default lead at a moderate clip before the pace quickens sharply from two furlongs out, turning this into a flat-out sprint where positional advantage is decisive; horses that travel prominently without burning energy early are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Closers Denied
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Jag or another default leader goes forward at a genuine pace and sustains it on the good-to-firm surface.
scenarios.body: A true gallop on fast ground stretches the field out and catches the genuine hold-up horses — redistributed to midfield but lacking a true prominent-race profile — cold; the winner is likely one who travels in the top half of the field and has the tactical speed to go with the leader entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to set up a genuine late run for the horses mapped toward the rear end of the field.
scenarios.body: Due Date's best form at Yarmouth and good-to-firm going fits this scenario, and Tom Marquand is adept at producing a late challenge; however, with so many horses redistributed from a true hold-up position, the finishing surge risks being blunted by a field that is bunched rather than strung out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Headgear/Class Edge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the race is tight throughout and a horse with a fitness or headgear edge picks off rivals in the final strides.
scenarios.body: Blindfold Games (tongue-strap, George Boughey's 5/20 T14 form showing stable in reasonable nick) or Rianka (tongue-tie, competitive recent form at this course and distance) could benefit if the race resolves into a narrow photo; both ran at Yarmouth recently over 6f on similar ground and carry the leanest weights in the field.

watchPoints.text: Havana Jag is the default pacemaker in a field with no confirmed front-runner — if Kaiya Fraser allows it to bowl along unchallenged, its consistent placed record on good-to-firm gives it a genuine chance of lasting home.

Due Date's redistribution from true hold-up to midfield masks a horse that genuinely needs strong pace to deliver its best — watch for Tom Marquand adjusting tactics aggressively if the gallop is slow.

One For Harvey returns after 287 days off with a trainer in poor recent form (0/5 T14); any market support should be treated with caution given the hold-up style mismatch and lack of race fitness evidence.

Blindfold Games is the only runner with a directly comparable placed run at Yarmouth over 6f on good ground — if the race resolves into a close finish, its course-and-distance form gives it a marginal edge over rivals whose best form is elsewhere.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this 6f race despite the declared going of Good — runners proven on quick ground (Havana Jag, Blindfold Games, Rianka) hold a small advantage over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces.

races.name: Yarmouth Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roi de Coeur
runners_data.note: Course-confident horse who won over 8f on Standard at Yarmouth and now steps into a strongly-suited role as lone front-runner; Marco Ghiani rides and Marco Botti's yard is 4/20 in the past 14 days, though sim-going form (0W0P from 4 runs) is a mild flag worth noting.

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Dual winner over 7f and 8f on Standard ground, Ed Dunlop's runner returns from 55 days off which is the longest break in the field and must be considered; Tom Marquand's booking is an upgrade but the hold-up style means Chapman's Peak needs more pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Consistent form on Good ground — 1W2P from five similar-going starts — and a recent win over 8f at Goodwood (1/8f/GOO) establishes him as the most relevant recent form horse; Billy Loughnane rides for a trainer with a 1/10 short-term strike rate, and the prominent style means he slots directly into the race's most favoured position behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground (1/8f/GOO) and has placed at the track-relevant going before, so the conditions are not a concern; J F Egan partners for George Margarson whose yard is 0/8 in the past 14 days, and the hold-up style leaves this runner dependent on a stronger pace than Roi de Coeur seems likely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Roi de Coeur is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner mile handicap, and with no rival willing to dispute the lead, he can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits him on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth. Celtic Chariot will press close up from a prominent position, creating a small but tightly grouped shape rather than a strung-out field. Chapman's Peak and Guest House will settle in behind, though with only four runners the gaps will be compressed and the race is unlikely to develop into a true test of stamina. The race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a controlled, sustainable gallop — firmly favours prominent racers and those who can produce a sustained mid-race move rather than a late swooping finish from far off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roi de Coeur Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the field lacks the will to close him down in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Roi de Coeur dictates every stride and simply needs to find enough in the tank turning for home, where his recent Yarmouth win over this trip (1/8f/STA) underpins his course-and-distance credentials; Celtic Chariot, racing prominently just off the leader, is best placed to challenge if Roi de Coeur weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Chariot tracks Roi de Coeur throughout and applies sustained pressure from two furlongs out, grinding down the leader on the run to the line.
scenarios.body: Celtic Chariot's recent winning form over 8f on Good ground (1/8f/GOO) and a trainer in Kevin & Lauren Frost with a recent 1/10 strike rate suggests the horse is ready to capitalise on a strong finishing position; pressing a lone leader at Yarmouth's straight mile means the prominent runner only has to out-stay the front-runner rather than find a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely too strong and the field dramatically strings out, leaving Chapman's Peak or Guest House to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Chapman's Peak's two previous wins over 8f on Standard suggest he can travel smoothly if the pace obliges, and Tom Marquand's ability to time a run is a relevant jockey factor; however, with only four runners and a single front-runner likely to set a modest gallop, the distance from the front to the hold-up horses is unlikely to open up enough for a late swoop to be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Gallop Bunched Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur sets an extremely pedestrian tempo causing all four runners to race on each other's heels into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish over the final two furlongs at Yarmouth would neutralise pace advantages and introduce a significant element of luck in running, but this requires an unusually slow early pace that Roi de Coeur, racing prominently by habit, is unlikely to set; Guest House's form on Good ground (1W2P) offers some hope but his sim-going stats are mixed.

watchPoints.text: Roi de Coeur sets the pace entirely alone — if he is not pressed and Yarmouth's straight mile allows him to control the gallop, he could prove very difficult to peg back despite modest sim-going stats.
Chapman's Peak returns from 55 days off and, if not fully wound up after the break, the hold-up style offers little margin for error in a four-runner race with limited pace to chase.
Celtic Chariot is the only runner combining prominent style with solid Good-ground form at the mile trip — if Roi de Coeur ties up in the final furlong, Loughnane only needs to press a button.

With just four runners the field will be compacted throughout; Guest House and Chapman's Peak have nowhere to hide if Roi de Coeur's pedestrian gallop fails to create the gaps their hold-up styles require.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race — all four runners are tagged going=OK, but Celtic Chariot's 4/5 record on similar ground makes him the standout beneficiary of the underfoot conditions.
